newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mostly up as US mogas counters Asia.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mostly up as US mogas counters Asia.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly slightly firmer on Tuesday as some areas saw follow through buying after Monday's big price jump.
Dealers said Asia was showing signs of weakness on gas oil and heavy fuel but the U.S. remained very strong on gasoline.
Brent crude CFDs edged another couple of cents higher after gaining up to 15 cents a barrel on Monday.
The balance of this week talked around eight cents over July with the next three weeks talking six cents and three cents above and then three cents under respectively.
The 27-30 May week traded at flat with July soon after the open and later talked three cents over.
Gasoline edged up $1 a tonne having gained $5 a tonne on Monday.

June was pegged around $204.50 with July some $4.75 lower and physical barges trading at $201.50 and $202.25. Crack spreads were unchanged at $4.10 a barrel and $3.10 for the third and fourth quarters respectively.
Dealers were uncertain about what impact recent gains in the U.S. might have have.
Some expected up to 300,000 tonnes to move across the Atlantic while others saw at least three cargoes of unsold German gasoline still looking for U.S. buyers.
Heavy fuel was mostly little changed although some traders saw June barge swaps about $1 a tonne lower.
Dealers said the weakness reflected lower Rotterdam barges which traded between $84 and $85 amid poor bunker demand.
Jet premiums were little changed with June and July at $20 a tonne and $22 a tonne above the IPE respectively.
Gas oil crack spreads held at $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97) and $4.75 (1Q98).
Dealers said they saw strong selling pressure in Singapore with the third quarter asking $24.70 a barrel compared to June at $25.30.
